best_for: Teams and home-lab users who run their own Seafile server, or pay for SeafilePlus Cloud, and want folders on their computers to stay in sync with it.
description:
Seafile is open-source file sync and share software from Seafile Ltd. This desktop client, licensed under Apache-2.0, links your computer to a Seafile server so the folders you keep there stay the same on every machine you use.

What you sync also shows up in the server's web interface. There you can view and edit many file types in the browser, protect share links with a password and an end date, and bring back an earlier version of a file. Seafile's homepage also lists custom file properties, tags in parent and child groups, table, Kanban, gallery and map views, SeaDoc for writing documents together in real time, and an AI chat that answers questions about what is in your files.

points.title: A client, not a service
points.text: This app syncs files with a Seafile server. You need one: your own, your employer's, or the hosted SeafilePlus Cloud.

points.title: Server costs
points.text: The Community Edition server is free and open source. Pro is free for up to 3 users, USD 100 a year for 9 users, then USD 48 per user per year from 10 users. SeafilePlus Cloud Team is USD 8 per user per month with 500 GB of storage. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Sync client or drive client
points.text: This app keeps a full local copy of each library you sync. Seafile's separate drive client, SeaDrive, shows server files without downloading them all, which helps on small disks.

points.title: Sync controls
points.text: You can sync existing folders, sync only some sub-folders, set libraries as read-only, change the sync interval, exclude files and set a proxy.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is community-built
points.text: Flathub does not mark the Flatpak as verified, and it is on 9.0.20 while Windows and macOS are on 9.0.22. Seafile's help site has its own Linux install guides.

points.title: Install details
points.text: Windows gets a 64-bit MSI that installs for all users. The Mac build is universal. The Windows listing keeps 25 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
